posts.title: Poetry: Can the Malawian speak?
posts.description: CAN THE MALAWIAN SPEAK? By Dr. Suryaraju Mattimalla I am a Malawian. I was born in Malawi, On African soil, Under an African sky, With an African face, An African heart, And an African soul. But they invaded my race. They chained my race. They enslaved my race. They took my race from Malawi To their brutal Arab Muslim countries, Where they butchered my African race. Tell me, world, Must an African remain silent Because his pain is uncomfortable? Must a Malawian hide his tears To protect the reputation of the Islamic brown race? Must my African blood become invisible? Because powerful people refuse to see it? Can the Malawian speak? Alex Haley wrote Roots: The Saga of an American Family, A fictional work about an African family’s suffering in the West, A story of generations, A story of broken families, A story of stolen names, A story of stolen freedom. posts.title: Malawi’ Scorchers beat Albania in China tournament opener
posts.description: …Malawi 4-3 Albania… YONGCHUAN-(MaraviPost)- Malawi’s Scorchers have started their campaign at the Chinese Football Association (CFA), Team China International Women’s Football Tournament with a thrilling 4-3 victory over Albania in Yongchuan, China, on Saturday. The match was played at Yongchuan Sports Centre Stadium in Yongchuan District, Chongqing Municipality, as the Scorchers opened their campaign with an important victory in the four-nation competition. Speaking to MaraviPost Sports Desk after the match, Scorchers coach Randy Waldrum said there was still important work to be done, particularly in strengthening the team’s defence ahead of the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil. Waldrum’s assessment comes after his side conceded three goals against Albania, despite finding the net four times to secure maximum points in an entertaining encounter. posts.title: Malawi Former President Joyce Banda shares family joy
posts.description: LILONGWE — (MaraviPost) — Former President of Malawi Dr Joyce Banda has shared a heartwarming family moment as she prepares to witness the traditional engagement ceremony, popularly known as Chinkhoswe, of her adopted daughter, Rita Nyaude, and her fiancé, Noel Mkukumila. In a social media message published on Saturday, November 28, 2026, Banda revealed that she was spending the morning with some of her favourite family members as preparations gathered momentum for the special occasion. “Today, the 28th November, as we wait to witness my adopted daughter’s Chinkhoswe (Rita Nyaude & Noel Mkukumila), I am spending the morning with some of my favourite family members,” Banda wrote. President Joyce Banda shares family joy Her message captured the excitement surrounding the anticipated ceremony while offering the public a glimpse into her personal life away from the demands of national leadership and politics.
